title: Group Policy – Personal Trading in Non-Perpetual Securities (extract applicable to RE Services staff)

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employee includes an employee, director (other than a non-executive director), contractor or representative of Perpetual, when trading in Securities other than Perpetual Securities (e.g. Metrics Income Opportunities Trust units and other third-party securities) in a Personal Capacity.

tiers.name: Non-executive Directors of Perpetual
tiers.description: Non-executive directors of Perpetual are excluded from this policy; only the prohibition on Insider Trading applies to them.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Any person (including spouse, partner or financial dependent) or entity (corporation, trust, superannuation fund) over whose trades the Employee can exercise control or influence the investment decision.

rules.detail: No derivatives-specific rule or clearance regime. Securities is defined to include exchange traded and OTC derivatives, so trading a put/call over non-Perpetual securities is caught only as 'trading' generally and is permitted provided the Employee does not hold Inside Information, is not front running, and is not procuring a third party to circumvent the policy.
rules.evidence: exchange traded and OTC derivatives and contracts for difference (CFD)

rules.detail: No hedging definition or hedging-specific rule anywhere in the document.
Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not mentioned.
Short selling is not named or otherwise addressed.

CFDs are expressly named within the Securities definition; trading them is permitted subject to the same general insider trading, front running, conflicts and high-volume-trading restrictions, with no separate clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: exchange traded and OTC derivatives and contracts for difference (CFD)

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the document.
Granting security, charges, liens or pledges over securities is not mentioned.
Secured financing arrangements of any kind are not addressed.

No holding-period or buy/sell-window rule. A soft reputational restriction discourages frequent trading (daily trading is 'high volume') because of the impact on professional duties, but does not prohibit or set a minimum holding period.
rules.evidence: personal trading in securities on a daily basis is considered high volume as it would interfere with an Employees daily work

clearance.evidence: The following requirements and restrictions apply to all Employees: 1. PROHIBITION ON INSIDER TRADING ... 2. PROHIBITION ON FRONT RUNNING ...

short_term.evidence: personal trading in securities on a daily basis is considered high volume as it would interfere with an Employees daily work

external_documents: RE Services Personal Trading in Non-Perpetual Securities Policy (RE Policy) – full policy of which this document is an extract
Group Policy – Personal Trading in Perpetual Securities (governs trading in Perpetual's own securities, not applicable to MOT)

bespoke_clauses.clause: This document is Perpetual Limited's internal staff conflicts-of-interest policy governing 'RE Services' personnel trading in securities other than Perpetual's own (i.e. third-party and client-fund securities, which would include Metrics Income Opportunities Trust units). It is not a bespoke director/officer dealing policy issued by or for the Trust or its responsible entity, contains no closed periods, no preclearance system, and no scheme-specific carve-outs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no clear, dedicated regime addressing whether a director or senior executive connected with the Trust may enter a funded collar over their MOT holding; any restriction would have to be found in the generic insider trading, front running and conflicts prohibitions rather than in tailored dealing rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to hedging, monetisation, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing of any securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar with a bank-secured loan is not restricted by this document at all, so a bank cannot rely on it for comfort that the structure is permitted, only that it is not expressly prohibited.

summary: This is not a bespoke securities trading policy for Metrics Income Opportunities Trust; it is an extract of Perpetual Limited's staff policy on personal trading in securities other than Perpetual's own, applicable to 'RE Services' personnel (which would include staff dealing in MOT units). It contains no closed periods, no preclearance or notification system, and no rules on hedging, derivatives, monetisation, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing; OTC derivatives and CFDs are only captured because the Securities definition names them. A funded collar over vested MOT holdings is therefore not expressly prohibited, but is only constrained by the general prohibitions on trading while in possession of Inside Information, front running, and procuring third parties to circumvent the policy, none of which specifically addresses collar or financing structures. Because the document does not govern MOT directors or executives dealing in MOT's own securities as such, a bank should treat the collar as unaddressed by any tailored trading policy and rely instead on general insider trading law and case-by-case sign-off from Perpetual/the Trust's compliance function.
